about: Txomin Etxaniz is one of the historic names of Getaria txakoli, the lightly sparkling wine of the Basque coast west of San Sebastián. The Txueka family has records of winemaking in Getaria going back to 1649, and in the 1980s Iñaki Txueka helped revive local txakoli and create the Getariako Txakolina appellation in 1989. The family, with Andrés Txueka as winemaker, farms about 35 hectares of terraced slopes above the Bay of Biscay, where apple and pear trees grow among the vines.

The rosé is made from Getaria’s two native grapes, the white Hondarrabi Zuri and the red Hondarrabi Beltza, grown on steep hillside vineyards close to the Atlantic and trained high on pergolas and trellises to keep the fruit aired in one of Spain’s wettest wine regions. Fermentation is in stainless steel at low temperature with native yeasts, and the wine is bottled young so that it keeps a touch of its own natural carbon dioxide, the gentle prickle txakoli is known for.

The winemaker’s notes for the 2016 describe a pale, bright pink wine with strawberry, lime, white flowers and minerals, then tangy red berry and citrus with a hint of white pepper and a strong mineral return on the finish. In Getaria txakoli is traditionally poured from a height to wake up the bubbles, and it is the local partner for grilled fish and anchovies.
facts: Stainless steel, native yeasts, low temperature; slight natural carbonation
About 35 ha of terraced, Atlantic-facing slopes, vines 30+ years old
